correctness.rationale: Every local update is an involutive linear transvection. Conjugacy under cyclic scan rotation and commutation of nonadjacent leaf updates reduce every order to a two-hub cyclic gap. Explicit hub/leaf-parity equations are verified algebraically, and the four parity cases determine the full map order, fixed-space dimension, and rank of the squared-map difference. The resulting Jordan decompositions yield primitive cycle counts and the exact scan-frequency law. Two independent executable checkers support the symbolic proof: all 695,472 state-order pairs for k<=5 and 20,640 matrix fixed-space equalities through k=40. The proof handles k=1 and k=2 separately via the same valid formulas and does not extrapolate from finite checks.

value.rationale: A natural one-edge modification switches from bipartite K2k to a graph with k triangles. The theorem shows complete linear-dynamical invisibility of that edge when k is odd, versus deterministic switching of every schedule between order-two and order-three orbit populations when k is even. Exact normal forms, primitive orbit populations and labelled schedule frequencies explain a nontrivial, all-size spectral boundary; this is an essential structural classification, not an arbitrary small numerical table.
